title: Counit-normalized derived scalar mates respect geometric composition
statement:
Let $Z\xrightarrow{g}T\xrightarrow{f}S$ be morphisms of schemes with small pro-etale sites [def-weil-pbc-proetale-site]. Let $a_S:A_S\to B_S$ be a map of sheaves of commutative rings and pull it back to $T,Z$ using the canonical inverse-image compositors. Use ordinary unbounded derived categories of module sheaves, equivalently internal module objects [def-weil-sheaf-of-modules-category, def-weil-abstract-derived-category, def-weil-pbc-internal-abelian-sheaf-module-equivalence]. For $V=S,T,Z$ put $T_V=B_V\otimes^L_{A_V}-$ with its representative-normalized scalar adjunction [lem-pur-sheaf-ring-derived-coefficient-adjunction]. For every geometric map $h$ among these maps and their composites, use the canonical adjunction $h_R^*\dashv Rh_{*,R}$, $R=A,B$ [def-weil-pbc-proetale-operations]. Let $\lambda_h:h_B^*T_{\mathrm{target}}\xrightarrow{\sim}T_{\mathrm{source}}h_A^*$ be the balanced tensor/pullback comparison. On a flat-term K-flat representative $P$, it is represented by
$$h_B^*(B_{\mathrm{target}}\otimes_{A_{\mathrm{target}}}P)\longrightarrow B_{\mathrm{source}}\otimes_{A_{\mathrm{source}}}h_A^*P.$$
Write $\theta_h:T_{\mathrm{source}}h_A^*\xrightarrow{\sim}h_B^*T_{\mathrm{target}}$ for the scalar-adjunction mate of the inverse-image/scalar-restriction square [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization]. Define $\beta_{h,K}:T_{\mathrm{target}}Rh_{*,A}K\to Rh_{*,B}T_{\mathrm{source}}K$ as the $h_B^*\dashv Rh_{*,B}$ adjunct of $T_{\mathrm{source}}(\varepsilon^A_{h,K})\circ\lambda_{h,Rh_{*,A}K}$.

Then $\lambda_h=\theta_h^{-1}$, so this specified $\beta_h$ is precisely the geometric-adjunction mate of $\theta_h^{-1}$. With the canonical adjunction-compatible derived direct-image compositors $\kappa_R:R(fg)_{*,R}\xrightarrow{\sim}Rf_{*,R}Rg_{*,R}$ [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons], for every $K\in D(A_Z)$,
$$\kappa_{B,T_ZK}\circ\beta_{fg,K}=Rf_{*,B}(\beta_{g,K})\circ\beta_{f,Rg_{*,A}K}\circ T_S(\kappa_{A,K}).$$
Under the canonical identity comparisons $\beta_{\mathrm{id}}$ is the identity. In particular, for any commuting scheme square $j:U\to X$, $q:V\to U$, $p:Y\to X$, $j':V\to Y$ with $jq=pj'$, and a ring map $A_X\to B_X$ pulled back to the square, the same normalized compositors identify
$$Rj_{*,B}(\beta_{q,K})\circ\beta_{j,Rq_{*,A}K}=Rp_{*,B}(\beta_{j',K})\circ\beta_{p,Rj'_{*,A}K}.$$
This is an equality for the specified counit mates; no properness, openness, boundedness, flatness or invertibility of any $\beta$ is assumed.

proof.text:
Apply [lem-sfb-kflat-scalar-comparison-normalization] to each of the geometric inverse images with the transported rings. Its hypotheses hold because the sites are small and the source rings are the inverse images of the target rings. Its ordinary comparison is precisely the balanced comparison used to define $\lambda_h$, and its representative assertion identifies its derived inverse with the specified scalar-adjunction mate. Consequently $\lambda_h=\theta_h^{-1}$ on the entire unbounded derived category, not just on a bounded subcategory. Invert its composition identity, with geometric order $Z\xrightarrow gT\xrightarrow fS$, to obtain
$$\lambda_{fg}=(\lambda_g f_A^*)\circ(g_B^*\lambda_f)$$
under the canonical pullback compositors. Its identity assertion gives $\lambda_{\mathrm{id}}=1$. The normalization theorem requires neither flatness of the ring map nor exactness of scalar extension.

proof.text:
For the component calculation put $L_R=f_R^*$, $M_R=g_R^*$, $U_R=Rf_{*,R}$, $V_R=Rg_{*,R}$ for $R=A,B$, and $E=T_S$, $F=T_T$, $G=T_Z$. Work in the endpoints identified by the specified compositors: $(fg)_R^*=M_RL_R$ and $R(fg)_{*,R}=U_RV_R$. This is notation for transport along those isomorphisms, not a replacement adjunction. The adjunction-compatibility assertion of [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons] says explicitly that the composite counit is
$$\varepsilon^{R,fg}_H=\varepsilon^{R,g}_H\circ M_R(\varepsilon^{R,f}_{V_RH}).$$
By the mate definition, $\beta_h$ is natural and satisfies
$$\varepsilon^{B,h}_{T_{\mathrm{source}}H}\circ h_B^*(\beta_{h,H})=T_{\mathrm{source}}(\varepsilon^{A,h}_H)\circ\lambda_{h,Rh_{*,A}H}.$$
This is exactly the transpose used in the definition of $\beta_h$ in the statement, so it is the mate of $\theta_h^{-1}$. Equality of two candidate components can be tested by this counit transpose, since the adjunction hom correspondence is bijective.

proof.text:
Fix $K\in D(A_Z)$ and set $X=EU_AV_AK$ and
$$x=U_B(\beta_{g,K})\circ\beta_{f,V_AK}:X\longrightarrow U_BV_BGK.$$
Its transpose under the composite $B$-adjunction is
$$q=\varepsilon^{B,g}_{GK}\circ M_B(\varepsilon^{B,f}_{V_BGK})\circ M_BL_B(U_B\beta_{g,K})\circ M_BL_B(\beta_{f,V_AK}).$$
Naturality of the $f$-counit at $\beta_{g,K}:FV_AK\to V_BGK$ reads
$$\varepsilon^{B,f}_{V_BGK}\circ L_BU_B(\beta_{g,K})=\beta_{g,K}\circ\varepsilon^{B,f}_{FV_AK}.$$
Substitute this equality and then the defining transpose equation for $\beta_f$ from step 2. Functoriality gives
$$q=\varepsilon^{B,g}_{GK}\circ M_B(\beta_{g,K})\circ M_BF(\varepsilon^{A,f}_{V_AK})\circ M_B(\lambda_{f,U_AV_AK}).$$

proof.text:
Use the defining transpose equation for $\beta_{g,K}$ to replace the first two factors in the last display by $G(\varepsilon^{A,g}_K)\circ\lambda_{g,V_AK}$. Naturality of $\lambda_g:M_BF\to GM_A$, at $\varepsilon^{A,f}_{V_AK}:L_AU_AV_AK\to V_AK$, gives
$$\lambda_{g,V_AK}\circ M_BF(\varepsilon^{A,f}_{V_AK})=GM_A(\varepsilon^{A,f}_{V_AK})\circ\lambda_{g,L_AU_AV_AK}.$$
Thus
$$q=G\bigl(\varepsilon^{A,g}_K\circ M_A(\varepsilon^{A,f}_{V_AK})\bigr)\circ\lambda_{g,L_AU_AV_AK}\circ M_B(\lambda_{f,U_AV_AK}).$$
By the $A$-counit formula in step 2 and the inverted normalization identity in step 1 this is
$$q=G(\varepsilon^{A,fg}_K)\circ\lambda_{fg,U_AV_AK}.$$
It is the specified transpose of $\beta_{fg,K}$. Injectivity of the composite adjunction hom bijection gives equality. Returning to the original endpoints inserts precisely $\kappa_B$ after $\beta_{fg}$ and $E(\kappa_A)$ before $x$, which is the displayed composition equation in the statement. The calculation used naturality and composition only and never inverted a $\beta$.

proof.text: For an identity geometric map the normalized adjunction and both geometric functors are the identity by [lem-sfb-ringed-derived-monoidal-comparisons]. Also $\lambda_{\mathrm{id}}=1$ by step 1. Its defining counit transpose is therefore $1\circ1=1$. Under the identity adjunction the transpose map itself is the identity, so $\beta_{\mathrm{id}}=1$.

proof.text:
For the square write $h=jq=pj'$. Apply the composition equation first to $(j,q)$ and then to $(p,j')$. The first path is
$$\kappa_{j,q,B}\circ\beta_{h,K}\circ T_X(\kappa_{j,q,A}^{-1}),$$
and the second is
$$\kappa_{p,j',B}\circ\beta_{h,K}\circ T_X(\kappa_{p,j',A}^{-1}).$$
Both therefore become the single arrow $\beta_{h,K}$ when their endpoints are identified with $T_XRh_{*,A}K$ and $Rh_{*,B}T_VK$. These are exactly the normalized identifications specified in the statement, including the coefficient-ring identifications from $h^{-1}$. In particular the assertion is an equality after these comparisons, without any assertion that either path is invertible. The argument works for every commuting square; no cartesian-square, open-immersion or properness hypothesis has been used. The Lean implementation composes each component equation with the inverse B-compositor, cancels hom followed by inv, and uses equality induction on the given equality of Edge composites to account for both eqToHom transports.

proof.text: Implemented auxiliary restriction comparisons: the identity-on-sections isomorphism is the unique proEtaleRingRestrictionDirectImage. Its inverse geometric mate is proEtaleRingRestrictionPullbackInv, which is invertible. The derived hom-equivalence compatibility in lem-weil-pbc-ring-sheaf-change-adjunction identifies the exact localization of this action with the geometric mate of proEtaleRingRestrictionDerivedDirectImage. In both the ordinary and derived categories, taking the scalar mate after the geometric mate equals conjugation under the composite adjunctions (Mathlib iterated_mateEquiv_conjugateEquiv_symm). Conjugation preserves isomorphisms, proving ordinaryTheta and theta invertible without a K-flat argument or a flatness assumption on the coefficient map.

proof.text: Implemented coefficient and ordinary identity obligations: composition compatibility follows by naturality of the inverse-image ring compositor and the two coefficient-square equations; identity compatibility is naturality of the conjugate of lowerStarId. For each coefficient ring construct the ordinary direct-image identity using SheafOfModules.pushforwardCongr₂ along Over.pullbackId.symm, followed by pushforwardId. The required ring map is lowerStarId.inv by unit_conjugateEquiv_symm. Its composite with restriction along pullbackId.inv is the identity since pullbackId.hom and pullbackId.inv are inverse. The resulting module isomorphism has exactly the prescribed section formula. That formula proves uniqueness by extensionality.
